raw_response:
I am not going to spread myself too thin this year. On my 10.1 mu, I will keep most of the land in the wheat-maize rotation because that is the steady way here, and keep a smaller piece in cotton for extra cash. I have done this land for many years, and what matters to me is not chasing the highest yield on paper, but making sure I can afford the inputs and still bring grain home. Wheat and maize are the backbone. Cotton can make money, but it takes more watching and more sprays, so I will not put too much land there. I have well water, so if the season turns dry I can save the crop, but pumping costs money, so I will not irrigate carelessly.

For wheat, I will do about what usually works in the village: sow in early October, use a common improved seed, put base fertilizer before sowing, then topdress once when the wheat starts growing strongly in spring. If the leaves stay pale, I may lean a little heavier on nitrogen, but not too much because fertilizer is expensive. After wheat harvest in June, I will hurry to plant summer maize on the same land. The turnaround is tight, so I will keep tillage simple and use machine help if needed. For cotton, I will keep it on 3.6 mu. Cotton needs more labor and more pesticide attention, so I only keep what I think my family can manage well. I would rather do a manageable area properly than plant too much and fall behind.
